Check available guidance, tools or procedures to guarantee a correct answer. The files handbook.pdf, mes_log.csv, test_defects.csv and thermocouples.csv are saved under /app/data/.

diagnosed_skill_and_repair.overall_diagnosis: The task failed before any substantive reflow-profile computation completed: none of the required /app/output/q01–q05.json artifacts were produced. Across samples, the recurring issue is that the reflow-domain skills provide conceptual formulas and handbook-grounded computation guidance but do not sufficiently enforce an end-to-end operational workflow that extracts handbook limits, computes deterministic metrics from thermocouple/MES data, and writes schema-compliant JSON outputs. The agent also appears vulnerable to execution derailment from tooling/command issues and lacks explicit completion checks. Repairs should focus on turning the skills into prescriptive execution playbooks with deterministic config extraction, representative thermocouple selection, TAL interpolation, conveyor feasibility logic, output schema generation, rounding/sorting rules, and mandatory artifact validation.

skills.name: reflow-machine-maintenance-guidance
skills.heading: Suggest to get a config object from the handbook and use it for all computations.
skills.diagnosis: The skill emphasizes concepts, equations, and handbook terminology but does not sufficiently prescribe the benchmark’s required end-to-end execution flow. The agent failed to operationalize handbook retrieval, representative thermocouple selection, TAL/peak/ramp calculations, conveyor feasibility analysis, and generation of the five required JSON outputs. The absence of explicit sequencing, file-output requirements, validation steps, and environment/tool usage guidance likely contributed to complete artifact omission.
skills.repair_instruction: Add a mandatory 'Evaluation Protocol' section that explicitly sequences the workflow: verify /app/data inputs; extract numeric limits/definitions from handbook.pdf into a cfg object; load CSVs; compute Q1–Q5 deterministically; and always write /app/output/q01.json–q05.json even if values are null or partial. Include concrete guidance for representative thermocouple selection (cold spot/worst case), TAL interpolation, peak aggregation, ramp-region filtering, conveyor-speed feasibility equations, tie-break logic, handling missing TC data, and ranking best runs. Add terminal usage examples showing one command per execution or safe chaining with &&/;, plus a minimal Python template for reading data, computing metrics, rounding to 2 decimals, sorting outputs, validating JSON parseability, and writing files.

skills.heading: max metric
skills.diagnosis: The skill contains the deterministic computation framework needed for ramp, TAL, peak, and feasibility metrics, but it is not prescriptive enough as an operational benchmark playbook. It lacks explicit output contracts for q01–q05, schema/rounding/write-path instructions, completion checks, and sufficiently detailed integration guidance between handbook-derived config objects and thermocouple/MES processing. This likely allowed the agent to stall before generating outputs.
skills.repair_instruction: Extend the toolkit with explicit task-output contracts mapping computations to q01–q05 schemas, including mandatory file creation under /app/output/*.json, rounding to 2 decimals, sorting requirements, null handling, and final validation checks. Provide canonical implementations for handbook-config extraction, TAL segment interpolation above liquidus, max-ramp computation within handbook-defined regions, representative-TC/cold-spot peak selection, conveyor feasibility from heated length and speed, and best-run tie-break logic. Add a concise completion checklist emphasizing that successful execution requires all five JSON artifacts to exist and load successfully before termination.
